_comment: Independent reproductions of the Vaara conformance vectors: parties other
than the maintainer who ran the checkers and reported the result in public.
THIS IS A RECORD OF THINGS THAT HAPPENED, NOT A LIST OF CURRENT MEMBERS.
A run happened on a date at a commit. That does not stop being true later,
so a row does not come down later.
Rows are chained. Each carries `prev`, the digest of the row before it, so
removing or reordering an entry changes every digest after it. Verify with
scripts/vcr_chain.py, which imports no Vaara code.
WHAT THE CHAIN GIVES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. Rewriting or reordering a
published row changes every digest after it and anyone recomputing sees the
break. Removing rows from the END is a different thing: what remains is a
perfectly valid shorter chain, and a reader holding only this file cannot
tell. So removal is detectable relative to a RETAINED HEAD, and saying the
maintainer 'cannot' remove a row was an overclaim twice over. Iman Schrock
raised the first half on the SCITT list on 2026-08-21 and Emek Can Dogru the
second, that a truncated chain verifies clean. Both were right.
scripts/vcr_chain.py now states tailPinned on every run and carries it in
--json, so nothing downstream reads 'verified' as 'verified to be complete'.
--expect-count and --expect-last-hash let a reader who kept a head pin it,
and a mismatch exits the same way a mid-chain break does.
SO THE HEADS ARE WITNESSED. `witnessed_heads` below records each published
chain head in a public transparency log the maintainer does not operate.
A rewritten chain produces a head that matches no witnessed entry, and that
is checkable by anyone against the log rather than against a promise. The
residual is real and narrow: a row added after the last witnessing carries
only the chain until the next head is published.
WHAT A RUN ESTABLISHES IS A PROPERTY OF WHO WROTE WHAT. Every row names
its kind, and the three are not degrees of one another:
reproduction: the author's checkers over the author's vectors. It
establishes that the artefact runs and is byte-stable somewhere other
than the author's machine, and nothing about the specification text.
independent_implementation: written from the text, run against the
author's vectors. It establishes something about the text, because a
second reader had to decide what the sentences meant.
independent_implementation_and_vectors: an independent implementation
run against independently constructed vectors. It establishes
something about both.
A row that does not name its kind reads as the first one, because that is
the weakest claim available. Rows listed before the field existed carry no
kind and are never edited to add one, so the page states the rule instead.
Joel Hillier proposed this on the SCITT list on 2026-08-21, after Iman
Schrock scoped his own row that way with nobody asking him to. The loss it
prevents happens where a result gets filed: a row outlives the message
that explains it, and a register that cannot tell a reproduction from an
independent implementation gets cited for the second while holding the
first, by someone who is not lying.
Rules for a row:
1. The party is not the maintainer.
2. The report is public and linkable. No private mail, no screenshots.
3. The claim is quoted as they scoped it, never widened.
4. The party agreed to be listed, knowing the entry is permanent. Being
public elsewhere is not agreement to appear here.
5. Nothing is edited after the fact. A correction is a new row that
refers to the earlier one, never a rewrite of it.
WHAT AN OUTSIDE SUGGESTION CAN CHANGE. Wording changes when it is shown to
be false, and anyone may show that, including a party that competes with
Vaara. A case, an expected verdict or a checker changes only on evidence
that the current one is wrong, never on request and never to make a party
pass. Every such change is a commit anyone can diff.
A party asks for a row with the conformance-row issue form, which records
the agreement in rule 4 and cannot be submitted without it. The rendered
page is generated from this file plus the runner's own report, so neither
can drift from the other.
`terms_version` below is the version a new row agrees to. Bump it when the
terms on the page change, and never edit a published version in place.
Every row stores the version it was listed under, so a change reaches rows
added afterwards and never reaches back to somebody who agreed to
something else.
